DRFT-85: Build.bound/claim_url were marked deprecated in DRFT-84 (shipped
v0.9.0, 2026-08-21) and are removed here now that the N-2 compatibility
window has closed — three releases (v0.9.1, v0.10.0, v0.11.0) have shipped
since, and the CLI's first-ever public npm release (v0.1.0) postdates the
deprecation, so no installed client anywhere could depend on these fields.
Server-side, both were already dead/hardcoded since DRFT-80. See DRFT-85 for
the full compatibility analysis.

POST /v1/builds removed the required property `data/bound` from the response with the `200` status
POST /v1/builds removed the required property `data/bound` from the response with the `201` status

DRFT-124/DRFT-126: recordDeployment/recordVerification/getCurrentDeployment/
getDeployment removed outright, NOT via the deprecate-then-N2 process above —
see this file's header comment in oasdiff.yml for why that's a deliberate,
separately-justified exception rather than a broadening of it. Deploy-marking
and verification (DRFT-88/96/97/98) were scope creep away from the product's
actual thesis (the build-info file itself, spec §1) and are being cut
entirely, not superseded. First shipped in a tagged release 2026-08-21
(v0.9.0), five days before this removal; this is a pre-launch product with no
production customers, so — same "no installed client could depend on this"
substance as DRFT-85 above, just without a prior deprecation flag, because
there was no intent to keep the feature around long enough to warrant one.
See DRFT-124 for the full decision record.

POST /v1/deployments api path removed without deprecation
GET /v1/deployments/current api path removed without deprecation
GET /v1/deployments/{deploymentId} api path removed without deprecation
POST /v1/verifications api path removed without deprecation

DRFT-129: the shared `Build` response schema is loosened (repository_id/
visibility/ref/workflow become optional) and `BuildMetadata` value maxLength is
raised 1024→4096, so `POST /v1/builds` responses can (per oasdiff) now omit those
four fields and carry longer metadata values. This is a deliberate, pre-launch
spec §2.2a inversion ("confirm, don't derive", DRFT-129) to share one `Build` type
with the new `registerDeclaredBuild` operation, where a declared build genuinely has
no linked `repositories` row and thus none of those four fields. The loosening is
only observable through that new operation: on the existing `registerBuild` path
every response still carries all four fields (verified builds always do), and a
pre-DRFT-129 CLI can never receive metadata larger than the bounds its own request
was validated against (request side is still capped at 50 properties / 1024 per
value for it). Same "no installed client could depend on the old strictness"
substance as the removals above, without a deprecation cycle, because the contract
is relaxed, not removed — safe only pre-launch while the latest tag is still v0.x
with no production customers. See DRFT-129 for the full decision record.

POST /v1/builds the response property `data/ref` became optional for the status `200`
POST /v1/builds the response property `data/ref` became optional for the status `201`
POST /v1/builds the response property `data/repository_id` became optional for the status `200`
POST /v1/builds the response property `data/repository_id` became optional for the status `201`
POST /v1/builds the response property `data/visibility` became optional for the status `200`
POST /v1/builds the response property `data/visibility` became optional for the status `201`
POST /v1/builds the response property `data/workflow` became optional for the status `200`
POST /v1/builds the response property `data/workflow` became optional for the status `201`
POST /v1/builds the `data/metadata/additionalProperties/` response property's maxLength was increased from `1024` to `4096` for the response status `200`
POST /v1/builds the `data/metadata/additionalProperties/` response property's maxLength was increased from `1024` to `4096` for the response status `201`

DRFT-165: `Build.repository_name` becomes optional (it was required), because a
local build (attribution `declared`, registered from a laptop with no CI) is never
attributed to a repository and so has no repository name; it is attributed to the
registering person instead (new optional `Build.registered_by`). Relaxation, not
removal, and the same pre-launch substance as DRFT-129 above: on `POST /v1/builds`
(`registerBuild`) every response still carries `repository_name` (a verified build
always has a repository), so the loosening is observable only through
`registerDeclaredBuild` and `listBuilds`, where a declared build can now appear.
The CLI never reads `repository_name` from any response (it writes build-info.html
from the build id and resolution URL), so no installed client depends on the old
strictness. Safe only pre-launch while the latest tag is still v0.x with no
production customers. See DRFT-165 for the full decision record.

POST /v1/builds the response property `data/repository_name` became optional for the status `200`
POST /v1/builds the response property `data/repository_name` became optional for the status `201`
GET /v1/orgs/{slug}/builds the response property `data/items/items/repository_name` became optional for the status `200`
POST /v1/orgs/{slug}/builds the response property `data/repository_name` became optional for the status `200`
POST /v1/orgs/{slug}/builds the response property `data/repository_name` became optional for the status `201`

DRFT-165 (revised): `Build.attribution` (verified | declared) is removed and
`Build.registered_by` changes from a string to an object `{kind, email?}`. Who
registered a build is now one identity with a kind, a CI pipeline (`workload`) or a
signed-in person (`user`), instead of a verified/declared label plus an email, so
the vocabulary that let a laptop build be mistaken for a pipeline one is gone from
the wire. Same pre-launch substance as DRFT-124/126 above (sanctioned reason 2):
`registered_by` as a string existed only in v0.19.0, which no deployed server
returned; and the CLI never reads `attribution` from any response (it writes
build-info.html from the build id and resolution URL), so no installed client
depends on either. Safe only pre-launch, while there are no production customers.
See DRFT-165.

POST /v1/builds removed the required property `data/attribution` from the response with the `200` status
POST /v1/builds removed the required property `data/attribution` from the response with the `201` status
POST /v1/builds the `data/registered_by` response's property `type` changed from `string` to `object` for status `200`
POST /v1/builds the `data/registered_by` response's property `type` changed from `string` to `object` for status `201`
GET /v1/orgs/{slug}/builds removed the required property `data/items/items/attribution` from the response with the `200` status
GET /v1/orgs/{slug}/builds the `data/items/items/registered_by` response's property `type` changed from `string` to `object` for status `200`
POST /v1/orgs/{slug}/builds removed the required property `data/attribution` from the response with the `200` status
POST /v1/orgs/{slug}/builds removed the required property `data/attribution` from the response with the `201` status
POST /v1/orgs/{slug}/builds the `data/registered_by` response's property `type` changed from `string` to `object` for status `200`
POST /v1/orgs/{slug}/builds the `data/registered_by` response's property `type` changed from `string` to `object` for status `201`

DRFT-165 (CI-only registration): `registerDeclaredBuild` (POST /v1/orgs/{slug}/builds)
is removed outright and `Build.registered_by` with it. Letting a person register a build
from a laptop required resolving a self-typed `owner/name` to a repository record, which
put unproven repository names beside ones an OIDC token proved; that breaks the trust
boundary the challenge flow exists to hold, so the path is cut rather than superseded.
Every build is now registered by a CI pipeline (a workload OIDC token is the only
credential `registerBuild` accepts), so `registered_by` carried no information beyond
the existing `provider`. Same pre-launch substance as DRFT-124/126 above (sanctioned
reason 2): `registerDeclaredBuild` shipped in v0.x with no production customers and no
declared builds exist in staging or prod; `registered_by` as an object existed only in
v0.20.0, which no deployed server or CLI pins (both pin v0.19.0). `listBuilds`
(GET /v1/orgs/{slug}/builds) is dashboard-tier and unchanged; it shows up below only
because the strip step leaves the removed POST's path in the base side. The `Build`
fields loosened by DRFT-129/165 are required again, which only tightens responses.
Safe only pre-launch, while there are no production customers. See DRFT-165.

POST /v1/builds removed the required property `data/registered_by` from the response with the `200` status
POST /v1/builds removed the required property `data/registered_by` from the response with the `201` status
POST /v1/orgs/{slug}/builds api path removed without deprecation
GET /v1/orgs/{slug}/builds api path removed without deprecation
